questions.stem: A 56-year-old postmenopausal woman comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of worsening pain and swelling in her left knee. She has a history of peptic ulcer disease for which she takes cimetidine. Examination shows palpable crepitus and limited range of motion of the left knee. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for this patient’s symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Celecoxib

Celecoxib is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID). It works by reducing hormones that cause inflammation and pain in the body. Celecoxib is used to treat pain or inflammation caused by many conditions such as arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and menstrual pain.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 222.

questions.stem: Among the following options, Lasmiditan belongs to which class?
questions.solutionHtml:
5HT 1 F Agonist

Lasmiditan

  • Lasmiditan is used to treat the symptoms of migraine headaches (severe throbbing headaches that sometimes are accompanied by nausea and sensitivity to sound and light). Lasmiditan is in a class of medications called selective serotonin receptor agonists.
  • Serotonin 1F agonist is Lasmiditan and is used for the acute treatment of migraine, with or without aura, in adults, agonist at 5HT 1 F receptor & inhibits descending pain pathway

    Toxicity: dizziness, vertigo


Lange Katzung's Basic and Clinical Pharmacology- 15th Edition, Chapter 16, Page Number: 28, 35

questions.stem: Among the following options, which drug belongs to PG F2 alpha?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dinoprost

PG F2 Alpha (Natural Prostaglandin), Dinoprost is a medicine used to induce labour in women, who are ready to deliver a full-term baby. It works by softening and widening the cervix (lower end of the uterus) and helps the baby to pass through easily.



Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 206

questions.stem: Among the following options, which prostaglandin is given by inhalational route?
questions.solutionHtml:
Treprostinil

May be administered by subcutaneous/intravenous infusion or by inhalation or also by oral, Treprostinil and Iloprost is given as an inhalation in pulmonary HTN, Treprostinil, is a vasodilator that is used for the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension. Treprostinil is a synthetic analogue of prostacyclin (PGI 2 ).



Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition Chapter 37/Page Number: 683

questions.stem: The effect of aspirin on urate excretion, if it is taken 5 g/day is?

options.label: A
options.text: Urate retention and antagonism of all other uricosuric drugs

questions.solutionHtml:
Increased urate excretion

The effect of low-dose aspirin to inhibit urate excretion may result from aspirin-induced inhibition of urate secretion by the proximal tubule. Paradoxically, much larger doses of aspirin (>3 gm/day; or over ten 325 mg tablets/day) have been observed to be uricosuric (increase urate elimination in the urine)

questions.stem: Aspirin should be used with caution in the following groups of patients because of which of the following reason?

options.label: A
options.text: In diabetics because it can cause hyperglycemia

options.label: B
options.text: In children with viral disease, because of the risk of acute renal failure

options.label: C
options.text: In gout, because it can increase serum uric acid

options.label: D
options.text: In pregnancy, because of the high risk of teratogenicity

questions.answerText: In gout, because it can increase serum uric acid
questions.solutionHtml:
In gout, because it can increase serum uric acid
  • At therapeutic doses, Aspirin can cause hyperuricemia by decreasing the excretion of uric acid. It, therefore, should not be used in patients with gout. It also decreases the uricosuric action of probenecid.
  • At high doses (>5 g/d), it increases the excretion of uric acid, but such high doses are not tolerated.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 214, 215

questions.stem: A patient who is on aspirin drug for some condition presented to your clinic. Among the following effects, aspirin intake can cause an increase in which effect?
questions.solutionHtml:
Bleeding time

Bleeding time is a medical test done on someone to assess their platelet function. It involves making a patient bleed, then timing how long it takes for them to stop bleeding using a stopwatch or other suitable devices

Uses of Aspirin

  • As analgesic (300 to 600 mg during 6 to 8 h) for headache, backache, pulled muscle, toothache, neuralgias.
  • As antipyretic in fever of any origin in the same doses as for analglesia. However, paracetamol and metamizole are safer, and generally preferred.
  • Acute rheumatic fever. Aspirin is the first drug of choice. Other drugs substitute Aspirin only when it fails or in severe cases.
  • Antirheumatic doses are 75 to 100 mg/kg/24 h (resp. 4-6 g daily) in the first weeks.
  • Rheumatoid arthritis. Aspirin a dose of 3 to 5 g/24 h after meal is effective in most cases. Since large doses of Aspirin are poorly tolerated for a long time, the new NSAIDs (diclofenac, ibuprofen, etc.) in depot form are preferred.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 214
